articles.title: 8GB 显存即可运行：5.8B 图像生成模型 FLUX 3 Image Klein 发布
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，视觉人工智能实验室 Black Forest Labs 当地时间本月 15 日以开放权重的形式发布了 FLUX 3 Image Klein 图像生成模型。FLUX 3 Image Klein 拥有 5.6B 的参数，针对消费级 GPU 进行了优化。其 BF16 权重需要 12.2GB 内存、FP8 权重则需要 5.6B 内存。这款模型的 INT8 版本可通过 ComfyUI 或 Diffusers 在仅配备 8GB 显存的 NVIDIA GeForce RTX GPU 上运行。根据测试，精简后的 INT8 版本在 GeForce RTX 5090 上生成 1MP 的图像大约需要 4s，在 GeForce RTX 4070 上通过 ComfyUI 生成 1MP 图像不到 9s。FLUX 3 Image Klein 支持文本转图像、图像编辑、多参考生成，原生支持 4K 分辨率，可实现像素级精确编辑和稳定的图案限位表现。Black Forest Labs 称在多个场景下优于尺寸更大的开源模型，在速度-质量平衡上具备更好的表现。参考https://bfl.ai/blog/flux-3-image-klein

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，2026 世界智能网联汽车大会于 2026 年 10 月 21 日至 23 日在北京亦庄举办。据汽车黑科技报道，吉利控股集团董事长李书福谈及吉利与蔚来合作换电，称是为了不重复建设。李书福表示，同样的道理，智能化也应该协同起来，减少重复投入，只有大而强才能引领行业。据IT之家此前报道，9 月 28 日，蔚来与吉利控股集团达成充换电领域全面战略合作。双方达成技术、运营、资本全方面合作共识，将联合投资双方充换电业务主体公司，共享充换电技术与标准，共建充换电服务网络。吉利控股集团将以其持有的易易互联 100% 股权及现金 6.4 亿元入股蔚来能源，交易完成后，吉利控股集团将持有蔚来能源 30% 股权，易易互联营运车辆换电业务将并入蔚来能源，蔚来能源将持续提升营运车辆换电网络的运营，赋能易易互联营运车辆业务；双方将共建统一的 C 端换电技术和标准，吉利控股集团将开发面向 C 端的换电车型，蔚来能源将为吉利控股集团 C 端换电车型提供服务。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋今天在柏林的 GTC 大会表示，未来所有电信运营商都将提供 AI 算力，电信基站有望发展成分布式 AI 网络。IT之家注意到，黄仁勋在发布会现场重提了 AI“五层蛋糕”理论，即是将人工智能从下至上划分为能源、芯片、基础设施、模型和应用五个层级。他强调 AI 不仅是软件，而是像电力和互联网一样的底层工业基础设施，各层之间紧密相连、向上拉动。他还指出，AI 这个大蛋糕包含西门子能源、施耐德电气等能源企业，以及 AI 工厂建设商 Nscale 和 Firebird，以及欧洲 AI 模型公司 Mistral、法律 AI 公司 Legora 和翻译工具 DeepL 等。

articles.title: 蔚来李斌：用户不愿意付钱，自动驾驶讲得再好也没有真正创造用户价值
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，今日，蔚来创始人、董事长、CEO 李斌在 2026 世界智能网联汽车大会的对话环节中提出，自动驾驶进入“下半场”后，衡量其价值的标准需要回到两个可以被验证的指标上。李斌将这两个指标概括为：用户是否愿意为自动驾驶功能付钱，以及自动驾驶能否让用户显著感知到它比人开车更安全。他直言，如果用户不愿意付钱，自动驾驶讲得再好，也没有真正创造用户价值。李斌此前曾多次解释蔚来坚持辅助驾驶订阅模式的逻辑：辅助驾驶背后存在履约、训练、通讯和升级成本，企业如果没有收入来源，服务本身便不可持续。在今天的发言中，他将“用户愿意付钱”直接定义为下半场的核心指标之一，意味着自动驾驶的竞争正在从功能展示转向可持续的商业验证。另一个指标指向安全性的可量化与可感知。李斌没有停留在“更安全”的笼统表述上，而是给出了蔚来辅助驾驶的累计运行数据：辅助驾驶里程超过 91.4 亿公里，使用时长超过 1.12 亿小时，避免和减轻事故超过 907 万次。他同时引用了保险机构的数据：经四家保险公司联合评估，2026 年上半年蔚来主动安全系统使用户事故安全损失降低 38.4%，人车共驾的安全里程达到单人驾驶的 8 倍。这一减损比例此前已在 2026 世界新能源汽车大会上由蔚来披露，当时的统计节点为 2026 年上半年，避免或减轻事故的数字为超过 850 万次，此次大会更新至 907 万次。在李斌的框架中，明年 7 月 1 日《智能网联汽车自动驾驶系统安全要求》强制性国家标准（GB 44721—2026）的实施，是自动驾驶进入下半场的重要标志。该标准由工业和信息化部组织制定，适用于搭载 L3 级和 L4 级系统的 M 类与 N 类车辆，要求自动驾驶系统的安全水平至少达到合格且专注的驾驶人的水平，并对人机交互、用户告知和检验检测体系提出了系统性要求。在李斌看来，合规划定了底线，但并不自动等同于用户价值；技术方向正在向“世界模型加闭环强化学习”收敛，L2 到 L5 在技术架构上同源，真正拉开安全上限差距的是冗余设计、算力规模和传感器配置。相关阅读：《华为靳玉志：以真实数据建立用户信任，是自动驾驶规模化商用落地的关键》《华为靳玉志谈自动驾驶进入“下半场”》《蔚来李斌：与吉利在很多方面都有讨论合作，良性竞争不是内卷》

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，绿联宣布推出升级款 11 合 1 USB4 扩展坞，型号为 U500，售价 699 元。这款扩展坞为 11 合 1 多口设计，总共享带宽可达 40Gbps，其中 USB4 下行接口带宽为 20Gbps，支持 8K 60Hz / 4K 240Hz 视频输出，同时可提供 7.5W 充电。网络方面，这款扩展坞内置 2.5GbE 高速有线网口，可自适应 2500/1000/100Mbps；供电方面，这款新品支持 PD 3.1 协议，总输入最高 140W，其中 USB4 上行口可给笔记本提供最高 115W 供电，USB4 下行口可给手机平板提供最高 7.5W 供电。产品拥有双色指示灯，白色指示灯表示 USB4 模式（双屏显示），橙色表示 DP alt 模式（单屏显示或无显示），短按开关即可控制扩展坞开关机；额外配备一根 Type-C 转 DP  连接线，可快速连接 DP 显示器。IT之家附这款新品详细参数：京东绿联 U500 USB4 扩展坞 699 元直达链接京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 12306 回应女子错过检票下跪哀求：停检后无例外放行通道
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，昨日，一段女子在火车站检票口情绪失控、下跪哀求工作人员放行的视频引发关注并登上微博热搜。据大风新闻、河南法治报等媒体报道，事发时该女子在发车前几分钟才赶到检票口，但已经超过了车站规定的发车前 5 分钟停止检票时限，检票员依规未予放行，并建议她尽快办理改签。现场画面中，女子反复哭求“还有 2 分钟，我都到这里了”，随后当众下跪。围绕“为什么不能再通融两分钟”，12306 客服的回应是：停止检票后，无论列车是否已经驶离，都不存在例外放行的通道。当然，这一规则并非广州东站独有，而是全国铁路检票作业的通用逻辑。光明网援引长春火车站的信息指出，停止检票时间由各车站根据客流、站台距离、列车类型等因素制定，常见范围为开车前 3 至 5 分钟，此时检票口屏幕会切换为红色字体显示，提示旅客已停止进站。百度百科收录的铁路运输资料进一步说明，停检时长没有全国统一标准，开车前 2 分钟、3 分钟、5 分钟、7 分钟的情形均存在，八达岭长城站因地下站结构复杂，提前 12 分钟即停止检票，精河站则因检票后需换乘摆渡车前往站台，停检时间提前至 15 分钟。各站“量身定制”的依据，是检票口到站台的实际通行距离和站场布局，目的是确保旅客有足够时间安全登车，而不是在发车前最后一刻在通道或电梯上抢行。从铁路作业的角度看，停止检票后的几分钟并非单纯的“等待时间”。发车前，站台客运员需要清空安全白线并向列车长发出信号，列车长完成关门防夹自检后再将数据上传调度系统，列车才能获得发车许可。如果在闸机已经关闭后破例放行，旅客在通道或站台上奔跑、扒门，都可能触发列车的紧急制动，进而影响同一线路上后续列车的正常运行秩序。同时，错过检票并不意味着车票完全作废。据 12306 现行规则，列车开车后，旅客仍可在票面当日 24:00 之前，在车票发站且有余票的前提下，免费改签当日其他同方向列车，仅能办理一次改签。如果当天所有车次都已无票，系统还设有改签候补通道，车站服务台也提供退改协助。退票则必须在开车前办理，一旦过了票面开车时间，退票通道即告关闭；如果列车已经停止检票、但尚未到开车时间，此时办理退票需收取 20% 的退票费。当然，IT之家不建议将“停止检票时间”视为出行的硬截止节点，大家应按照铁路部门建议至少提前 25 至 30 分钟抵达车站，为安检、步行至检票口和站台留出余量。相关阅读：《短视频博主传授所谓“候补购票小妙招”，12306 回应称从未与第三方合作》

articles.title: 斯巴鲁 2027 年底前在欧洲停售燃油车，全面转向纯电
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，斯巴鲁近日向外媒《Auto Motor und Sport》确认，公司最迟将于 2027 年在欧洲停售燃油车，全面转向电动汽车。据报道，斯巴鲁在欧洲的市场份额并不算高，去年仅售出 2.3 万辆，市场份额为 0.2%。该公司将于今年年底在欧洲停售 Outback，并于 2027 年陆续让 Impreza、Crosstrek 和 Forester 等车型退出欧洲。从 2028 年开始，斯巴鲁在欧洲只提供三款车型，全部都是纯电动汽车：Solterra、E-Outback 和 Uncharted。这些汽车均为丰田合作研发，分别基于 bZ4X、bZ4X Touring 和 C-HR+ 打造。斯巴鲁表示，公司在欧洲全面转向电动汽车是因为当地政府的二氧化碳排放、辅助驾驶规范限制。欧盟近期规定，2025 年至 2034 年生产的汽车，平均每公里二氧化碳排放量必须控制在 93.6 克以内，较 2021 年的水平降低 15%。IT之家注意到，斯巴鲁的下一代电动汽车将采用自主研发技术，不再使用丰田共享的技术。新一代平台将配备全新电池、电机技术，以及支持通过无线方式更新软件的集成控制单元。

articles.title: 法国两家苹果零售店遭洗劫：里尔门店一度暂停营业，波尔多门店曾在 2018 年遇袭
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，据 MacRumors 今日报道，法国多地近日发生示威活动，期间波尔多和里尔的两家苹果零售店遭到洗劫。据法新社（AFP）报道，2026 年 10 月 17 日，法国多个城市发生商铺遭破坏和洗劫事件，波尔多、里尔等地的零售商店受到波及。其中，波尔多的 Apple Sainte-Catherine 门店此前也曾在 2018 年 12 月法国“黄背心运动”（不满油价持续上涨）示威期间遭到洗劫。此次事件中，两座城市的多家商铺同样成为袭击目标。法国媒体 MacGeneration 报道称，里尔苹果门店位于法伊德赫布街（Rue Faidherbe），波尔多门店则位于圣凯瑟琳街（Rue Sainte-Catherine）。当地媒体和现场影像显示，有人进入门店并带走商品。不过，两家门店具体损失金额以及被盗设备数量目前尚未明确。苹果里尔门店在事件发生后暂时关闭，波尔多门店也调整了营业安排。据法国科技媒体 iPhoneAddict 10 月 19 日报道，里尔门店当时计划于 10 月 21 日恢复营业，波尔多门店则已重新开放，但营业时间有所调整。苹果尚未就两家门店遭洗劫一事公开发表评论。法新社报道称，除苹果门店外，多个城市的服装店、食品零售店、运动用品店、奢侈品门店和通信设备商店也遭到破坏或洗劫。例如IT之家注意到，知名电子竞技俱乐部 Team Vitality 巴黎总部于 10 月 18 日遭洗劫，导致奖杯和电脑设备被盗，所幸无人受伤。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，2026 墨甲机器人全球发布会今日在安徽芜湖举行。墨甲机器人总经理张贵兵表示，墨甲机器人全球销量已超过 3000 台，覆盖 100 多个应用场景；产品与服务已进入 60 多个国家和地区。奇瑞集团旗下墨甲机器人正式发布其首款消费级家庭陪伴人形机器人墨宝，同步开启全球预订。墨宝身高 0.9 米，圆润曲线和柔性材料增强亲和感，22 个自由度支持行走与身体表达。IT之家获悉，墨宝可为孩子提供识物问答、故事和英语互动，为长辈提供日常陪聊及按用户设定的事项提醒，并通过家庭成员识别与长时记忆延续交流。产品支持 20 多种语言互动。据介绍，墨宝以空间感知层理解环境，以交互层承接语言、手势等表达，以执行层完成身体运动，以决策和认知层负责任务编排与记忆，形成感知、决策、执行和反馈闭环。在长期陪伴方面，墨宝分层管理事实、经历和经验记忆，并通过 FaceID 关联用户身份，约束专属记忆调用。MogaCloud 支持任务下发与 OTA 更新，符合回流条件的数据经端侧脱敏和安全校验后进入云端学习与验证，推动能力持续完善。京东 AiMOGA 奇瑞墨甲 墨宝 Mobo 智能机器人预定权益包 99 元直达链接京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 奔驰与英伟达合作开发城市辅助驾驶系统 MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO，计划年底在德国向部分用户开放
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，梅赛德斯-奔驰今日宣布，旗下 MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO 城市辅助驾驶系统计划于 2027 年上半年在德国开放订购，并于 2026 年底率先在斯图加特和慕尼黑向部分符合条件的客户开放。该系统由奔驰与英伟达合作开发，支持从起点到终点的辅助驾驶，可协助车辆应对城市道路中的多种交通场景。据奔驰官方介绍，MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO 将导航与驾驶辅助功能结合起来，能够协助车辆完成变道、通过路口、识别红绿灯并进行启停等操作，即使在交通密集的城市道路中也可提供辅助。该系统通过车载传感器采集周围环境信息，并结合计算平台与驾驶辅助软件规划车辆行驶路线。该系统属于 SAE L2 级驾驶辅助系统，能够在驾驶过程中辅助控制车辆，但并不意味着车辆可以完全自动驾驶。驾驶员仍须持续关注道路状况，并随时准备接管车辆。技术合作方面，奔驰与英伟达围绕驾驶辅助系统开展合作，由英伟达提供人工智能技术、DRIVE AV 软件及 DRIVE AGX 计算平台。IT之家此前报道，双方还宣布扩大合作，计划共同开发下一代驾驶辅助与自动驾驶系统，相关技术将结合奔驰的 MB.OS 操作系统以及英伟达 Hyperion、Alpamayo Stack 和 Halos 等技术方案。相关阅读：《梅赛德斯-奔驰与英伟达深化战略合作，共同推动下一代辅助驾驶系统开发》

articles.title: Synaptics 推出 Astra SR200 MCU：内置谷歌 Coral NPU，集成高带宽定制 DRAM
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，边缘 AI 芯片企业 Synaptics（新突思）美国当地时间 20 日宣布推出 Astra SR200 系列 xMCU。这批产品在常规微控制器的基础上提供了可运行多模态边缘 AI 的能力。Astra SR200 系列采用异构 AI 原生计算与加速架构，搭载 Synaptics Torq AI 引擎，内置 Google Research 的 Coral NPU，集成容量可扩展至数百 MB 的高带宽定制 DRAM，可在设备端运行更大规模的 AI 模型和更丰富的多模态工作负载。Astra SR200 系列首次在业界采用 Arm Cortex-M85 与 Cortex-M52 的 CPU IP 组合，提供至多 400 GOPS 的 AI 算力，面向下一代 AI 可穿戴设备、电池供电传感设备、联网摄像头、流媒体设备、工业视觉和语音系统。Synaptics 还基于系列中 AI 算力最高的 Astra SR250 打造了 Coralboard SR 开发板，提供 microSD、NOR、MIPI-CSI / DSI、USB、Wi-Fi、蓝牙等支持。相关阅读：《谷歌推出 Coral Board 单板计算机：1 TOPS 算力，本地运行 Gemma 3 模型》

articles.title: 小鹏汽车董事长何小鹏称 L3 安全性没有变好，自动驾驶应该跳过 L3
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，据第一财经报道，小鹏集团董事长、CEO 何小鹏今日在世界智能网联汽车大会上表示，自动驾驶应该跳过 L3。L3 模式下安全责任转移给系统，但它只是转移了责任，用户体验没有优化，重点是安全性没有变好。他称未来 L5 会重新被定义，汽车自动驾驶属于被动式自动驾驶；而机器人是需要 24 小时主动执行任务的；过去 L5 是纯从技术维度定义的，没有从安全、场景可控角度去定义。何小鹏认为，各个国家监管体系想要管控自动驾驶、支撑技术向更高等级演进，一定要安全、可管控。基于这个逻辑判断未来自动驾驶赛道真正有发展机会的是 L2、L4 和重新定义后的 L5，而 L3 本质上只是 L2 的一种增强形态。据IT之家此前报道，在今年 3 月的一场沟通会上，何小鹏谈及“为何跳过 L3”时表示，L3 是接近 L2 的能力，责任主体还是在司机，L4 就会有一个新的不同的责任主体。他认为，在今天全球科技发展的情况下，L2 和 L4 中间专门加一个 L3，实际上对于硬件、软件、法律、法规都是挑战。相关阅读：《小鹏汽车 CEO 何小鹏：自动驾驶下半场将出现三个重大变化，以及三个核心指标》《何小鹏：L2 和 L4 之间专门加 L3，对于硬软件和法律法规都是挑战》

articles.title: 环路资本将苹果评级下调为“持有”，同步下调 iPhone 营收预期
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，据科技媒体 macrumors 今天报道，环路资本（Loop Capital）已将苹果股票评级从“买入”下调为“持有”。该机构认为，苹果不太可能弥补原定 2026 年下半年出货、但后来又从计划中削减的约 1,300 万台 iPhone。据报道，环路资本将苹果目标股价从 370 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 2,476 元人民币）下调至 330 美元（现汇率约合 2,208 元人民币）。此前该机构表示，内存和处理器短缺导致 iPhone 出货延期，苹果试图在 2027 年补回这部分销量。但根据最新供应链调查结果，环路资本不再认可这一判断。该机构还预测，苹果在 12 月的季度 iPhone 出货量约为 7900 万台，低于最初预估的 8500 万台。到了 2027 年，iPhone 全面出货量预计为 2.6 亿台，但平均售价更低，因此将 iPhone 营收预测从 3,150 亿美元（现汇率约合 2.11 万亿元人民币）下调至 2,850 亿美元（现汇率约合 1.91 万亿元人民币）。苹果广受关注的分批发布策略，也让其财务前景更难预测。iPhone 18 Pro 系列已于 9 月发布，iPhone Duo 将于 10 月 23 日上市，但 iPhone 18 标准版、iPhone 18e 和 iPhone Air 2 预计要到 2027 年春季才会推出。

articles.title: 上海国际航空枢纽战略规划发布：江苏南通新机场计划明年开工、2035 年建成
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，中国民航局在最新发布的《新时代新征程上海国际航空枢纽战略规划》中提出，上海正持续推进全方位门户复合型国际航空枢纽建设，计划明年开工建设江苏南通新机场，到 2035 年，将力争进入世界一流航空枢纽前列。《规划》中提出，江苏南通新机场计划明年开工，建成后将成为上海国际航空枢纽重要组成部分。浦东、虹桥、南通新机场将形成“两地三场”一体化运营和高效互联的综合交通体系，年客货吞吐量提升至 2 亿人次、540 万吨，建成具有全球影响力的世界级临空产业集群。IT之家获悉，按照分阶段目标，2030 年前浦东机场四期扩建工程将完成，2035 年南通新机场建成。

articles.title: 陕西神木警方回应问界汽车起火：系单方事故，司机已遇难
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，近日，一辆问界汽车在陕西榆林神木市一路口处发生碰撞起火。据新京报今日报道，神木警方称，该事故系一起单方事故，事发车上仅司机一人，已遇难。另据IT之家今日早些时候报道，问界用户服务官方发布了关于陕西省榆林神木市车辆事故的说明。经初步核实：事发时车辆处于人驾状态，行经至交汇路口时车速为 139.1km/h（事发路段限速 50km/h），因车速过高撞击路口方形的交通灯立柱后起火，起火位置为车辆前部。关于车辆起火原因，初步分析为高速情况下车辆机舱遭受剧烈撞击引发线路短路及油液泄漏，导致起火燃烧。目前问界方面正在全力配合相关部门开展事故调查工作，详细结论以官方最终调查结果为准。相关阅读：《问界发布关于陕西省榆林神木市车辆事故的说明：事发时车辆处于人驾状态，行经路口车速 139.1km/h》

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，因高压电池存在缺陷，大众汽车集团正在全球范围内召回约 7.27 万辆电动汽车。这已经是该公司今年以来至少第三次因电池问题发起大规模召回。德国联邦汽车运输管理局（KBA）召回数据库 10 月 20 日更新的信息显示，此次召回分三批次进行，仅德国境内就涉及约 1 万辆。受影响车型几乎覆盖了 MEB 平台纯电产品线的主力：大众 ID.3、ID.4、ID.7 和 ID.Buzz 涉及 2022 年至 2025 年生产的车辆，除此之外还包括西班牙子品牌旗下 2022 至 2024 年生产的 Cupra Born。大众方面表示，内部质量检查发现，部分高压电池电芯不符合质量要求。目前，缺陷产生的根本原因尚未完全查明。在极少数情况下，相关电芯可能导致电池热负荷升高，严重时存在车辆起火风险。作为临时安全措施，大众要求受影响车辆将充电上限限制在 80%，以降低电池热失控风险。车主将通过信函收到召回通知，随后需要前往授权经销商处检查高压电池。维修人员将根据检查结果判断是否需要更换电池电芯模块。大众还计划根据车辆生产周期、电池供应商和电芯批次，进一步明确受影响车辆的范围。这并非大众今年首次因高压电池问题召回电动汽车。今年春季，大众集团已在全球范围内召回近 10 万辆存在潜在电池问题的电动汽车，其中包括大众和 Cupra 的多款车型。德国及欧洲相关召回记录显示，部分电池缺陷可能导致异常自放电、热负荷升高，极端情况下存在起火风险。在美国市场，大众本月也宣布召回 22524 辆 2023 至 2026 款 ID.4 电动 SUV。根据美国国家公路交通安全管理局（NHTSA）的召回文件，特定充电模式与电池电量超过 80% 的情况相结合时，可能引发电池内部热传播，进而导致车辆起火。大众目前尚未确定最终维修方案，要求相关车主暂时将充电上限设为 80%。此次美国召回涉及的电池电芯供应商为 SK Battery America。汽车媒体 Electrive 报道称，大众在 2024 年 1 月至 2026 年 8 月期间收到 22 起相关索赔或投诉。此前，今年 1 月，大众还在美国召回了约 4.4 万辆 ID.4，原因涉及 SK Battery America 生产的电芯电极错位问题。IT之家提醒：目前欧洲此次涉及约 7.27 万辆汽车的召回与美国 ID.4 召回虽然都涉及高压电池安全问题，但大众尚未公开确认两者是否使用同一供应商的电芯，也未明确说明缺陷是否存在直接的技术关联。相关阅读：《大众因高压电池可能着火在美召回 22524 辆 ID.4 汽车》

articles.title: 靳玉志称自动驾驶对安全的要求会变得更高，重申华为引望电子螺丝钉定位
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，2026 世界智能网联汽车大会于 2026 年 10 月 21 日至 23 日在北京亦庄举办。据新浪汽车报道，在大会巅峰对话环节上，业内多位嘉宾共话全球自动驾驶如何进入“下半场”，华为公司高级副总裁、引望公司 CEO 靳玉志谈到：自动驾驶对安全的要求会变得更高。我们知道辅助驾驶 L2 级阶段的话，发生事故时责任主体还是在司机，但是到了 L3 级以上自动驾驶的时候，责任主体会转移到系统，转移到自动驾驶的系统，所以对安全的要求是变得更高。此外，靳玉志还重申了华为引望的“电子螺丝钉”定位。他表示，引望从诞生之初，一直都是坚持做智能网联时代的新增的智能化部件的供应商，形象地说我们提供了一个电子螺丝钉的角色。我们希望在全球能够做价值共创，因为自动驾驶要健康持续发展，不能仅仅是在中国，它一定是依赖于全球的车企伙伴，全球的协会标准，我们在政策法规、行业标准落地应用方面要进行共创价值共创。IT之家注意到，靳玉志在接受媒体采访时曾多次强调，引望始终坚持“电子螺丝钉”的战略定位，不和整车造车产生冲突，帮助车企造好车、卖好车，使华为乾崑真正成为汽车行业智能化的公共平台。相关阅读：《华为靳玉志：“境”和“界”并不冲突、是互补的关系，鸿蒙智行打造 30 万以上汽车的样板点》

Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are evolving from conversational assistants into Cowork Agents capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and complex task execution. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26904v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent studies have proposed reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) methods that enable LLMs to generate high-quality RTL circuits from natural-language specifications. Existing approaches optimize circuit PPA (Power, Performance, Area) by aggregating multiple objectives into a single scalar reward, making it difficult to simultaneously generate diverse Pareto-optimal solutions across different trade-offs such as low power, low latency, and small area. However, in practical design, the relative importance of each objective varies depending on product requirements and design constraints; thus, obtaining a diverse and high-quality candidate set is beneficial in that designers can choose a preferred trade-off a posteriori. articles.content:

Abstract: The adoption of Large Language Models for radiology report structuring has been largely dominated by either proprietary cloud-based models or large open models requiring high-end GPUs for deployment, which is a critical bottleneck for clinical adoption in radiology workflows that demand data privacy and offline operation. articles.content:

Abstract: General-purpose agents are increasingly expected to perform professional analytics work, which requires sustained reasoning, iterative investigation, and reliable evidence. Training these capabilities requires diverse and challenging tasks. The framework progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, then inherits and combines these workspaces to uncover deeper questions. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated theorem provers often rely on sampling language models, but proof assistants like Lean reject each failed step with a precise error message --- information that pure sampling discards. To overcome this, we introduce a bounded, online step-level repair module. Our search samples $K$ candidate tactics at each step and repairs a failed tactic at most $R$ times. Instead of discarding failed tactics, we feed the compiler's error message to a pretrained repair model to fix individual rejected steps in place. Abstract: Mathematical reasoning is a fundamental capability for educational applications of Large Language Models (LLMs), where reliable problem solving requires not only correct answers but also coherent and verifiable reasoning processes. articles.title: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26948v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conversational recommender systems have recently adopted vision-language models to match user dialogue intents with multimodal product information. However, extending these methods to many product domains faces a dilemma: deploying a separately adapted VLM per domain scales cost linearly with the number of domains and requires routing each dialogue to the right model, while naively merging all domains into a single VLM degrades accuracy because product characteristics vary widely across categories. We propose LightCRS, a lightweight, query-conditioned framework for unified multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendation. LightCRS precomputes multimodal product representations once offline with frozen encoders. articles.title: SPEM: Structure-Aware Procedural Memory for Efficient Skill Use in LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26995v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based agents increasingly rely on reusable skills. However, scaling skill libraries makes efficient and accurate skill use difficult. Full skill loading incurs high token and runtime overhead. In contrast, flat semantic retrieval treats skills as independent text entries, ignoring dependencies, execution order, state transitions, and data flow constraints. We propose SPEM, a lightweight structure-aware procedural memory framework for efficient skill use in LLM-based agents. SPEM maintains Atomic Skill Memory for individual skills and Skill-DAG Memory for reusable compositions derived from successful executions. For a new task, SPEM reuses high-confidence Skill-DAG templates when available. Otherwise, it retrieves atomic skills and invokes Skill-GNN for state- and structure-aware skill selection. Successful executions are written back as new Skill-DAGs, allowing procedural memory to accumulate over time. Experiments on ALFWorld and Sk

articles.title: Does Multi-Agent Collaboration Reduce Hallucination in Clinical Tasks?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27027v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems improve performance on clinical tasks, and that improvement is often read as evidence of a more trustworthy system. However, the two are not the same claim. A clinician acts on the stated reasoning and not only on the conclusion, so whether collaboration reduces hallucination, and what decides when it does, has to be measured in the reasoning too. Yet most evaluations score only the final answer. We evaluate four systems (a single-LLM baseline and three multi-agent topologies) across four models and three clinical tasks, scoring hallucination, under a factuality and faithfulness taxonomy, inside the rationale each system generates and reporting it alongside the task metric. We report that collaboration buys task performance but not lower hallucination as a rule, and no topology is reliably better than another. Abstract: A poker agent can make a legal move and still make a strategically poor one. We ask whether compact AI agents can exhibit strategic behavior under hidden information and whether preference optimization can improve beyond static and zero-shot policies. We first evaluate a static baseline and three frozen language models: SmallThinker, Qwen3, and Gemma-3 whose performance varies substantially between exact-game and six-player evaluation. We therefore propose Strategic Preference Optimization with KL-anchored Equilibrium (SPOKE), combining teacher-relative value penalties, policy anchoring, risk constraints, and structured rationale supervision, and compare it with SFT, DPO, GRPO, and GSPO. Across three runs of a SmallThinker-4B-A0.6B policy, SPOKE achieves the lowest mean exploitability in Kuhn (0.213) and Leduc (1.081) and the highest six-max top-1 agreement (0.775), while maintaining teacher KL comparable to SFT (0.522 vs 0.523). Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents have recently demonstrated outstanding performance in single-turn tasks, yet they continue to struggle with long-horizon tasks, particularly in environments without prior training. A key limitation of single LLMs is their difficulty in processing long contexts, which stems from weaknesses in continuous decision-making and reasoning capabilities. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27045v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In recent years, physical artificial intelligence (physical AI) has experienced rapid development, capturing significant attention in academia and industry. However, the field has yet to reach consensus on its definition, technical landscape, and core challenges. To address this gap, this monograph seeks to define physical AI, present its technical landscape, and examine each key technical subfield in depth. In doing so, it establishes a unified framework for Physical AI: artificial systems that perceive, model, and act upon the physical world through continuous feedback under real-world constraints. Further, this monograph distinguishes physical AI from conventional digital AI, embodied AI, cyber-physical systems, and digital twins. It develops the foundations of physical AI across physics, control, cognition, learning, and reasoning. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27046v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As AI systems begin to resolve open research problems, reliable verification becomes increasingly important. Formal mathematics provides a trusted framework for mathematical reasoning, enabling agents to produce machine-checkable proofs while conducting mathematical exploration. Existing formal mathematics benchmarks often focus on known results or a small set of prominent open problems, which can become difficult to evaluate reliably once solutions are discovered and widely disseminated. Existing evaluation protocols are also not always aligned with how modern coding agents operate. We therefore introduce ReuF2F, a Lean 4 benchmark of 244 formalized open problems drawn from Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), spanning entry-level open research problems across a broad range of mathematical subfields. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27099v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Clinical care, health-system operations and biomedical discovery depend on extracting reliable answers from patient records, yet applying diverse clinical questions across entire populations remains computationally expensive. Here we present Clinical System One (CS1), a 4-billion-parameter decision model for fast, typed judgments from clinical records, along with two agentic harnesses in which CS1 works together with a generalist language model. CS1-4B is trained on 12.4 million questions and answers from 3.6 million patients across a multi-hospital health system, combining structured-data keys, observed outcomes and language-model supervision across clinical notes, diagnostic reports and patient timelines. It answers multiple typed questions in a single forward pass without task-specific retraining, and each answer carries a probability that can route uncertain cases to human review. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27103v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent Omni LLMs (OLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in joint audio-visual reasoning, yet cross-modal hallucinations remain a major challenge. Existing mitigation methods mainly operate at the output level, overlooking the entanglement of grounding evidence and learned priors within fused representations. To address this issue, we propose Omni-Woodpecker (OWP), a training-free framework that shifts hallucination mitigation from output-level manipulation to conflict-conditioned representation rebalancing. Specifically, OWP first identifies cross-modal conflicts from complementary modality-specific views. It then employs orthogonal decomposition to separate grounding evidence from competing priors within the hidden states. Finally, OWP adaptively rebalances fused representations by suppressing misleading priors and restoring ignored evidence before decoding. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27115v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents act on the external world through tools and third-party skills, so a single executed action can cause irreversible harm. Existing defenses judge a proposed action without tracking whether its content comes from the user or from external sources such as tool outputs, and they judge it in isolation rather than against an available alternative, which forces a trade-off between security and utility. We present PROVISO, a controller that decides which action to commit after the agent proposes an action and before it is executed. PROVISO encodes trusted observations, external observations, the proposed action, and an alternative into provenance-typed memory, relates them through role-specific queries, and commits the action with the highest calibrated value learned from outcomes. articles.title: PORA: Learning When More Reasoning Pays Off for LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27119v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents perform tasks over multiple steps and revise their actions based on feedback. As the total reasoning budget is often limited and must support future steps, the agent must choose between short and long reasoning before each action. Longer reasoning may improve the final task outcome by preventing later errors, but it also uses budget capacity that may be needed for future decisions. This creates two challenges: estimating the downstream value of long reasoning and deciding when that value is worth using the remaining budget. We propose Paired Outcome-guided Reasoning Allocation (PORA), which learns this decision by comparing short and long reasoning from the same interaction state. During training, \method{} completes the task twice from each selected state, once with a short reasoning allowance and once with a long allowance, and compares their final quality and total processing to estimate when longer reasoning is valuable. Abstract: Pluralistic alignment requires AI systems to learn from diverse populations whose preferences may reflect heterogeneous or even conflicting objectives, and to personalize their behavior to individual users. Existing approaches in pluralistic alignment often assume access to annotator identities and rely on powerful pretrained representations to model individual preference variations. We propose Preference-PCA Pluralistic Learning (P3L), a novel framework for pluralistic alignment that jointly learns trajectory embeddings and the shared basis of preference directions via PCA decomposition from heterogeneous crowd feedback without requiring annotator identities. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in non-verifiable domains such as financial services, where they must interpret user intent, rewrite queries, and retrieve information under domain-specific constraints. Although reinforcement learning (RL) can train such agents from the consequences of their actions, recent successes largely rely on verifiable tasks with automatically computed binary rewards. In non-verifiable retrieval tasks, assessing query quality requires scarce subject-matter expert (SME) judgment that is inherently graded rather than binary. Abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) integrates domain specialists into a shared student, but determining how strongly each teacher should supervise remains challenging. Existing discrepancy-based allocation can assign strong supervision even when the student already matches or exceeds the teacher's task performance, since behavioral mismatch does not necessarily imply a remaining capability deficit. We propose Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (CA-MOPD), which combines specialist merging with capability-guided allocation to account for what the student has already learned. CA-MOPD first merges reinforcement-learning specialists into a strong student initialization, then uses verifier-estimated teacher--student capability gaps to adjust domain-level distillation strength. Abstract: Scientific foundation models increasingly operate on continuous phenomena, yet still use discrete residual computation. We ask whether pretrained residual transformations can support additional latent computation without expanding the backbone. To test this possibility, we introduce Continuum-LM, which reuses these transformations as dynamical operators in a continuous-depth language model. Its hidden states evolve through an ordinary differential equation evaluated by higher-order numerical integration, with solver order and step size controlling computation. Across eight scientific tasks, Continuum-LM trains stably and improves mean exact-match accuracy by 7.77 and 10.96 percentage points over discrete counterparts at the 0.6B and 1.7B scales, respectively. Abstract: We show that two-layer transformers trained to near-zero loss on a sorting task converge to one of two mechanistically distinct solution classes depending on their initialization. One solution class consists of solutions that do not use the second attention layer to sort, but also fail to length-generalize. The other, which uses both attention layers, length-generalizes perfectly, despite only being trained to sort sequences of a fixed length. Abstract: Latent world models let an agent plan in latent space. articles.content:

Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains a language model by sampling responses, scoring them with an automatic verifier, and updating the policy from the resulting rewards. The policy therefore receives direct learning signals only from trajectories that appear in its rollouts. Yet repeated sampling from the same policy can concentrate on similar reasoning paths, leaving useful alternatives unexplored under a fixed rollout budget. We introduce Activation-Space Exploration (ASE), an online method for diversifying training rollouts. By clustering activation differences between correct and incorrect responses to the same problem, ASE builds a structured bank of latent exploration vectors. Different vectors are then applied to subsequent rollouts to explore alternative reasoning paths. Abstract: The feature-extraction quality of pre-trained models sets the ceiling of downstream transfer learning, yet few-shot model selection remains difficult: supervised evaluation on scarce labels is unstable and yields fluctuating rankings. EGiME performs $K$-means clustering over all labeled and unlabeled samples, then combines two entropy terms: an inter-cluster entropy measuring global separability, and an intra-cluster entropy measuring the compactness of labeled anchors, fused through an inverse-frequency weight that emphasizes small clusters. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27078v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce Lookup-table (LUT)-aware Efficient Attention on FPGAs (LEAF). LEAF is the first nanosecond-scale LUT-aware transformer for FPGAs. Deploying transformers that are large enough to perform well, small enough to fit on an FPGA, and fast enough to meet the sub-microsecond timescales required by real-time systems such as those at CERN remains difficult, since the same attention mechanism that gives these models their high expressivity also makes them costly to implement in hardware. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27079v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) watermarking operates on the next-token distribution that evolves during generation. In streaming generation, each sampled token becomes part of the text and affects subsequent distributions. Embedding therefore proceeds with a changing host, unlike classical watermarking, which adapts embedding to an existing host signal. To accommodate this difference, we formulate a novel embedding framework for LLM watermarking based on two principles. We first argue that embedding should be adaptive, retaining the state of previous sampling decisions to better guide subsequent choices. We further argue that embedding should be host-dependent, using the current LLM distribution to constrain both token selection and state updates. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27107v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Credit card fraud is a significant problem for financial institutions, resulting in substantial monetary loss each year. Fraud patterns and methods are continuously evolving, with fraudulent transactions often disguised to resemble legitimate activity. Real world transaction data for fraud detection is severely affected by class imbalance making it harder to detect these transactions. Fraudulent transactions are rarely isolated. Accounts, devices, and other common attributes are often shared across fraudulent activity, revealing relational patterns that individual transaction features alone cannot capture. Graph-based approaches model these relationships explicitly. However, standard graph neural networks aggregate neighbourhood information uniformly, which can dilute the already scarce signal carried by fraudulent transactions and limit detection of camouflaged fraud. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27123v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models reduce computation through sparse expert activation, but deployment still requires storing a large number of expert parameters. We study post-training expert pruning using task-domain calibration data as a subset-selection problem: given a pretrained MoE layer, select a fixed number of experts that best reconstruct its original output. Exact subset search is combinatorial and becomes intractable for modern MoE models with many experts per layer. We develop OptEP, a scalable continuous relaxation that directly optimizes differentiable expert-selection variables, followed by a lightweight reconstruction-based update of the retained expert weights. Across multiple MoE architectures and tasks spanning mathematical reasoning and code generation, our approach improves over the strongest existing expert-pruning baselines, with absolute accuracy gains of up to 15.05% on Qwen3-30B-A3B, 14.55% on Qwen3-235B-A22B, 11

Abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is challenging long-held assumptions in active flow control. By learning directly from interaction with a flow, DRL agents can find actuation strategies for nonlinear, unsteady flows without explicit models, often exploiting mechanisms that classical control would not anticipate. High-speed flows are a demanding test of this promise: shocks, shock/boundary-layer interactions, transition, aerothermal loading and microsecond-scale dynamics strain both algorithms and hardware. Yet most demonstrations remain idealized, low-speed simulations with limited evidence of robustness, interpretability, transferability or experimental deployment. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27139v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We encounter a system through its responses, yet its state concerns how the system is. Predicting further responses promises knowledge beyond what is immediately observed. What that knowledge tells us about the system's state depends on what we mean by a state in the first place. We give this notion a model-relative meaning: a state is the complete response profile over a specified query universe, and configurations agreeing on every query are regarded as the same state. From this perspective, a learned state is understood through the distinctions between these profiles that it retains. Prediction concerns selected observations; recovery concerns the profile as a whole. We examine their relationship through query ambiguity, state-space geometry, and the choice of prediction targets. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26864v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gradient ascent (GA) is a simple language-model unlearning baseline, but it continues increasing forget loss after useful forgetting has occurred. This unbounded pressure can damage retained utility and make forgotten examples abnormally high-loss. The targets are estimated from matched non-member examples before training, so the base objective requires one forget-batch forward/backward pass per optimization step; our reported TOFU variant adds sparse retain replay every tenth step. We instantiate a one-sided objective for TOFU question answering and a two-sided objective for MUSE-News language modeling. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26865v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Retrieval-augmented speech translation improves rare terminology, but systems such as RASST still assume that users provide a glossary before each session. That assumption is inconvenient for live talks, while merging every domain into one growing glossary eventually places too many irrelevant terms in the same retrieval and prompt competition. We present AutoTerm-SST, an interactive system that removes session-time glossary upload and domain selection. It organizes a large offline terminology catalog into topic slices, matches recent streaming translation context to bilingual slice prototypes, and activates a compact multi-slice working set under fixed retrieval and prompt budgets. On five ACL and five ESO oncology talks, AutoTerm matches a known-domain reference in terminology accuracy (88.3% vs. 88.1%) and mWER-resegmented BLEU (45.09 vs. 45.19), while requiring no domain input. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26867v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern speech systems are evolving into ecosystems of autonomous speech agents that speak together, negotiate, and trade assets such as embeddings, spectrograms, or raw data. In such markets, sellers cannot reveal assets for evaluation due to privacy constraints, and buyers cannot price what they cannot test. Thus, we open-source WaveCommitments, an end-to-end design that pairs confidential asset valuation via Data Shapley inside a trusted execution environment with multivariate polynomial commitments. It enables selective openings and tamper-evident provenance to prove that a delivered asset matches the valuation while hiding everything else. Our extensive experiments across three known datasets and various tasks with state-of-the-art encoders, including Whisper, reveal that we speed up the best benchmarks by up to 20x while reducing their proof sizes by up to 39x. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26868v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ambivalence and hesitancy (A/H) are subtle behavioural states that can be expressed through both what a person says and how it is spoken. This paper presents an audio--text framework for video-level A/H recognition. Full-video transcripts and speech waveforms are encoded using pre-trained multilingual BERT and wav2vec~2.0, respectively, and projected into a shared representation space. Two stacked bidirectional cross-attention blocks allow linguistic tokens to attend to acoustic frames and acoustic frames to attend to linguistic context without requiring explicit temporal alignment. The resulting sequences are aggregated through masked mean pooling and combined using concatenation, element-wise products, and absolute differences for binary classification. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26888v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Mixture of Phonetic Experts based Low-Rank Adaptation (MoPE-LoRA), a parameter-efficient adaptation framework for accented English speech recognition. Recent mixture-of-experts approaches typically allocate experts per accent, implicitly treating accent identity as the primary axis of variation. In contrast, we organize adaptation along phonetic categories, motivated by the observation that accent differences are often expressed as systematic distortions of phoneme realization. MoPE-LoRA introduces a fixed set of six low-rank experts aligned with manner-of-articulation classes and performs frame-level routing through a hybrid mechanism that combines phoneme supervision with learned acoustic gating. Because the expert set is shared across accents, the model does not require accent-specific modules and naturally extends to previously unseen accents. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26926v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) possess broad factual knowledge and strong reasoning capabilities, but solving complex tasks also requires procedural knowledge about how to act. Existing approaches often represent procedural knowledge through trajectories or bundled skills, limiting flexible reuse across interaction histories. This paper introduces Procedural Atoms, fine-grained and independently applicable units that represent Intent, When, Do, and Avoid guidance. Building on this representation, we propose AtomSD, an Atom-guided Self-Distillation framework in which the learner continually extracts Procedural Atoms from its own successful trajectories and distills them into the evolving policy through Atom-conditioned supervision and task-reward optimization. Abstract: Large clinical language models often require multi-GPU infrastructure, limiting local deployment. We introduce CERTA, a decision-level statistical certificate that determines when a quantized model may substitute for its native BF16 reference and escalates decisions that cannot be certified to it. In the higher-power operational analysis, round-to-nearest 8-bit quantization at BF16 storage served 99.8-100% of held-out decisions across all eleven models; formal finite-sample guarantees were assessed separately using the exact split-sample procedure. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26952v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Relational triple extraction identifies entity relations from raw sentences without depending on entity type information. The performance of traditional methods is seriously degenerated by ``unseen'' entities, because these methods can't build contextual dependencies relevant ``unseen'' entities. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing a multi-granularity interaction network that leverages word-word, entity-relation, and head-tail interactions to capture deep semantic dependencies. By incorporating multiple iterations, the multi-granularity interaction network is effective to refine the representations corresponding to head and tail entities. It enhances the global semantic features associated with relational triples, aiding in the remediation of triples that may have been overlooked or omitted in earlier steps. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26955v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon language agents require compact memories that retain interaction evidence while preserving competing hypotheses about unobserved states. Although effective, many belief-state methods encode memory in discrete natural language, where repeated compression can omit evidence or prematurely discard plausible alternatives. We introduce LAMB, a recurrent framework for latent multi-hypothesis beliefs. A Common--Delta factorization combines a shared Common state for interaction evidence with weighted Delta components for competing hypotheses. Relative evidence from action-outcome predictions guides recurrent hypothesis updates without generating textual memory. A context-conditioned readout exposes hypotheses separately to the policy through a fixed-token belief prefix in the default configuration. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26972v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present SZED's submission to ArGuard 2026 Track A: Arabic hateful meme detection. The task has two parts: binary classification (A1) and fine-grained multi-label tagging (A2). For A1, we fuse MARBERTv2 and CLIP ViT-L/14 embeddings, comparing concatenation, self-attention, and ensemble heads. For A2, we use a multi-task label-attention architecture with per-class query vectors and an auxiliary head for cascade calibration. We reach macro-F1 = 0.7597 on A1 and 0.3142 on A2 (averaged over 10 active classes). We report reproducibility across runs, per-class error patterns, and the effect of cascade calibration on the long-tailed A2 label space.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26976v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish sharp degree bounds for Putinar sum-of-squares (SOS) certificates in terms of the positivity margin $\delta$. For any fixed Archimedean quadratic module with prescribed generators and any fixed bound on the degree of the objective, we prove a uniform certificate-degree upper bound of $O(\delta^{-1/2}\log^2(2/\delta))$ for normalized polynomial objectives. We show that this bound is sharp by constructing a matching lower-bound example in three variables, thereby establishing that the dependence on $\delta$ is optimal. These matching bounds also yield sharp worst-case convergence rates for the Lasserre hierarchy.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27047v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: EHR foundation models promise scalable clinical prediction across health systems, yet their deployment is constrained by a tokenization bottleneck. The same clinical concept can appear as different ontology codes, local identifiers, synonyms, or free-text descriptions, which standard EHR tokenizers treat as unrelated symbols. A model trained on MIMIC-III with a closed-vocabulary tokenizer can use only 13% of eICU events. Abstract: Long-video understanding often requires answering many questions about a single video whose evidence is distributed across extended temporal contexts. Conventional video-language models repeatedly encode frames or retrieve visual evidence for every question. Parameterized video memory offers a write-once alternative, but existing methods rely primarily on synthesized text and fixed adaptation configurations, leaving open where video knowledge should be written and how visual evidence should shape the memory. Abstract: Controllable object insertion provides a targeted approach to augmenting object detection datasets that require category--count fidelity, annotation alignment, and source-content preservation beyond visual realism. Several approaches have been proposed to address this grand challenge, but most suffer from different constraints in precise category--count requests and visual consistency, limited coordination across categories and instances, and poor localization of multiple objects of specific category and count. We design SceneP2F, a two-stage trainable framework that connects scene-aware joint planning with layout-aligned generation leveraging explicit instance-level layouts. SceneP2F consists of two novel designs. The first is ScenePlan which allocates one class-labeled query per requested instance, jointly predicts scene-compatible object centers, and separately estimates box sizes conditioned on the planned centers and scene context.

Abstract: An event camera emits events at a rate given by the scene motion, object texture, illumination, its own contrast thresholds, and other settings. Across the N-Caltech101 dataset, recorded by a single event camera, the event rate varies by roughly 26x. Abstract: When given an image and a text prompt, vision-language models (VLMs) can produce seemingly sophisticated text responses. To detect these hallucinations, certain methods interestingly leverage internal signals from the VLM as it generates the text response; potentially, these methods use the same signals that led to a hallucination to detect it. Our method first generates full-body human motion from text and scene context, then predicts trajectories for a small number of intentionally manipulated driver objects conditioned on the human motion. articles.title: Visual Task Modeling and Automated Planning for Humanoid Robots in Education of Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27162v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In robot-assisted education, a robot must understand how to complete a task in order to effectively guide a student through it. We present a novel method that enables a semi-autonomous, camera-equipped robot to recognise the task goal and plan actions to achieve it. Our work focuses on Shoebox Tasks, an activity commonly used in the education of individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Abstract: Diffusion policies with linearly composed scores have emerged as a promising approach to multitask robotic learning by combining separate factors to enable modular, task-wise adaptation, compositional generalization, and interpretable functional decomposition. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27242v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humanoid dexterous manipulation needs reference motions that are both semantically rich and kinematically feasible for the target robot. Text-conditioned hand-object interaction (HOI) generators supply diverse, language-specified demonstrations, but they synthesize motion in human (MANO) space. The embodiment gap is therefore deferred to post-hoc retargeting, where trajectories deployed on the robot can fail to maintain contact with objects and also degrade policy learning. Our key idea is that robot reachability should constrain the interaction trajectories while they are being generated. We present EmbodyHOI, which runs a differentiable inverse-kinematics (IK) solver for a specific humanoid embodiment inside the sampling loop of a frozen flow-matching HOI trajectory generator. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27271v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Walking without vision requires timely, unambiguous guidance, yet many wearable aids encode directions as audio or vibrotactile signals that users must translate into movement. We present XoNav, a four-actuator hip exoskeleton that renders guidance cues directly at the hip joints. It renders an Advance cue and two-level Braking cues through sagittal-plane actuators and two-level Steering cues through frontal-plane actuators. A bilateral LSTM-based gait-state classifier uses two thigh-mounted IMUs to identify gait states, enabling haptic cues to be delivered in coordination with the wearer's gait while suppressing them during standing. The classifier generalized to unseen users with recalls of 95.2-97.9%, with mean detection delays of 38.6 and 63.1 ms for stance-to-swing and swing-to-stance transitions, respectively. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27275v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Maximum clique and maximum consensus are widely used formulations for robust point cloud registration in robotics. Maximum consensus seeks one transformation that aligns as many matches as possible, while maximum clique selects matches through pairwise distance tests. Maximum clique is often used as a substitute for or an approximation to maximum consensus, with empirical evidence suggesting a close relationship. However, how closely the two formulations agree is not fully understood. We study this relationship theoretically. We show that a maximum clique can have arbitrarily large alignment error and be arbitrarily larger than the maximum consensus set at any fixed positive tolerance, and derive geometric conditions that bound this error. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27277v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are sensitive to visual corruptions, but knowing that a corruption is typically harmful does not establish whether removing it would benefit the current episode. Furthermore, when several corruptions co-occur, deciding what to correct requires understanding which ones contribute to failure risk and how much their removal would help. We define this problem as failure attribution. Detecting corruption presence alone cannot answer this question, as corruptions can be present but relatively harmless, while directly measuring removal benefits requires costly paired policy rollouts with and without the corruption present. articles.title: RadGeoLoc: Radar Geolocalization via Particle Filtering
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27310v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In real-time autonomous field applications, GNSS is often unreliable and inaccurate. A possible solution is localizing against a prebuilt map like a satellite image, as it is georeferenced and already surveyed. In this work, we localize a spinning radar measurement against overhead RGB imagery with a learned observation model. We use a radar representation pretrained by masked reconstruction and align it to features from a satellite image. A particle filter propagated by radar odometry proposes candidate poses, and our observation model provides a likelihood over these poses. We evaluate our method over 31 distinct routes, over 8 datasets spanning both urban and offroad conditions using only ground radar and a coarse local prior. We also examine the robustness over changing weather using repeated traversals over the same route over 13 months, in both urban and offroad conditions.

Abstract: The integration of dynamic legged locomotion and aerial mobility offers versatility that is deterred by challenges in payload distribution, actuation, and the contrasting requirements of both domains. Abstract: Accurate head immobilization is critical for medical procedures such as neuroimaging and intracranial radiation therapy, where even minor motion can compromise precision. articles.title: Refuses When Asked, Complies When Acting: A Runtime Safety Check for Robot Control Loops
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27350v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Frontier models can control robots through agent harnesses that loop on one question: what motion comes next toward the user's goal? We show that this default loop carries out harmful instructions. With GPT-6 Astra controlling a low-cost SO-101 arm through the Inspect Robots harness on three household tasks whose hazard is common knowledge, such as "put the knife in the toy basket", the policy refused 0% of 15 trials, attempted the harm every time, and completed it in 27%. Its one exit, give_up, is meant for goals that cannot be achieved, and it never cited the hazard. We add an optional runtime safety check to the loop: before the first motion, the model is asked whether it would carry out the instruction, given the same camera frames. The check would have stopped all 15 hazardous instructions, including the 4 that completed the harm, and flagged none of the 15 harmless controls. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27387v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Action-conditioned video generative models trained on successful, goal-directed demonstrations tend to ignore the commanded action, rendering a plausible expert-like future regardless of what is asked of them. We trace this failure to training data that lack sufficient action influence. We analyze this metric and prove that it upper bounds the action influence that any model trained on that data can express. Expert demonstrations, whose narrow action distributions let next states be predicted without attending to the action, set a low ceiling that no amount of model capacity alone can raise. Raising it requires collecting different data. We introduce Action Influence Maximization (AIM), an algorithm for actively collecting training data for improving dataset action influence. Abstract: Reliable quadrotor flight in disturbed environments requires predictive models that remain accurate as unmodeled aerodynamic effects change during deployment. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27472v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mobile legged robots offer unique advantages for on-site construction, including the ability to traverse unstructured terrain, climb stairs, and operate independently between spatially separated work zones. This paper presents a proof-of-concept system for autonomous brick stacking using a Boston Dynamics Spot quadrupedal robot equipped with a manipulator arm. The system operates between a supply area and an assembly area, using AprilTag fiducials for localization and autowalk missions for navigation. Target brick positions and orientations are specified in CAD software and exported directly for robotic execution. We evaluate placement accuracy through ten repeated assemblies of a curved four-layer wall comprising 14 wooden bricks. articles.title: HATCH: Hardware-Attested Task Chains for Verifiable Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27485v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Capability claims in robot manipulation are unverifiable, and existing leaderboards are each closed, simulated, or gameable. We propose HATCH, a robot escape room: an openly specified, physically replicable, sensor-scored, and unrehearsable benchmark. Tasks span five skill categories at three difficulty levels and are chained so that the sensor confirming one task's completion unlocks the next, turning a room into a single long-horizon evaluation. Success is confirmed by instrumentation rather than human judgment, scoring is embodiment-agnostic, and object placements are randomized by a run-day seed. Entrants submit attested self-runs (uncut video, sensor logs, and the seed), with occasional organized events for calibration. Task specifications, build guide, bill of materials, and scoring rubrics are released under an open license.

articles.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
articles.content: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. To train across many skeletons, we use a generative video editor to place animated 3D assets in scenes suited to their actions, curating the edits so their known motion remains valid. Together with human and robot video, this yields nearly 200K training pairs. Our evaluations demonstrate that our model animates diverse rigs from text more faithfully than video-first pipelines, and its motion responds to the surrounding scene. It also turns video into rig motion, rig motion into video, and enables keyframe-based control of the 3D motion. Videos and additional results are available on our project page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/.

articles.title: AEON: Unifying Video and 3D World Models
articles.content: Current world models for explicit world simulation typically follow two distinct pathways: (1) video generative models (e.g., Sora), which simulate realistic appearances but fail to preserve 3D consistency; and (2) 3D generative models (e.g., Marble), which generate geometrically consistent scenes but often yield static, less realistic observations. We present AEON, a unified framework that bridges video-based and 3D-based world models and combines the benefits of both. The key insight of AEON lies in a generative model that operates within the text- or image-conditioned video latent space while producing renderable 4D graphics primitives---specifically, 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS)---as the explicit world representation. We train a 4D reconstruction model to predict both 4DGS and camera poses from monocular videos, serving as our initialized 4D decoder. Furthermore, we design a domain adapter that translates generative video latents into reconstructive 4D latents through a distillation process on the video VAE. AEON naturally supports video-based world modeling by rendering 4DGS at predicted camera trajectories, and constructs a persistent 4D environment with scene dynamics for realistic world simulation. Consequently, AEON empowers a diverse range of world modeling applications and achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks. Project Page: https://weiqi-zhang.github.io/AEON

articles.title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering
articles.content: Game engines and coding agents can specify the layout, motion, and camera of a scene, yet turning such coarse structure into realistic video requires a renderer that follows the structure and completes the appearance it leaves open. Existing renderers are tied to the representation of one engine, need tens of denoising steps or a costly distillation of their own, and learn from conditions that are not aligned with their target videos. We present SolarRenderer, a structure-conditioned video renderer that adapts a frozen MiniMax-H3 33B backbone with two lightweight LoRAs. Structural videos enter the native reference pathway of the backbone at the positions of the frames they describe, without a type identifier and described only in plain text, so that a single control LoRA follows arbitrary structural representations. Starting from a pretrained four-step LoRA, structure-guided distribution matching renders in four steps, 12.3 times faster than 50-step sampling, while preserving the learned control. A block-causal variant extends the same design to streaming and renders 768p video in real time. To train the model, we build a frame-aligned corpus of 136K clips from game engines, simulators, and YouTube videos. Experiments on an in-distribution test set and a generalization benchmark of 16 structural representations show that SolarRenderer achieves state-of-the-art results across both, and generalizes to 11 unseen representations, including pose skeletons, drawings, and point clouds.

articles.title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
articles.content: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending them to domain-intensive mechanistic investigations remains challenging. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general grain boundaries (GBs). Although general GBs constitute the vast majority of real-world interfaces in polycrystalline materials, they remain understudied because their structural complexity and interfacial mismatch complicate experimental and modeling research. GBClaw integrates large language models (LLMs) into a modular architecture comprising an orchestrator, specialized agents, domain-specific tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory. Through dynamic replanning and iterative workflow refinement, the framework effectively connects systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, GBClaw characterized interfacial defect structures and identified diverse deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. Comparing boundary sliding with and without secondary GB misfit dislocations revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of defect hierarchies in sliding resistance. Furthermore, researcher-guided follow-up calculations traced an anomalously high shear resistance to metastable boundary structures. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening with deep physical understanding of complex material interfaces.

articles.title: Learning Adaptable Dexterous Skills via Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking
articles.content: Dexterous multi-finger hands hold promise to unlock diverse skills like functional grasps, in-hand reorientation, and dynamic handover that the human-designed world assumes, yet existing learning recipes force a trade-off. Goal-reaching reinforcement learning generalizes to arbitrary object poses but, lacking any human prior, converges to unnatural and unreliable finger strategies; motion tracking reproduces human-like behavior from a single clip but cannot deviate from it. We present AdaDex, a goal-conditioned RL framework that turns a single hand-object trajectory of a few seconds---from mocap data or HOI reconstruction from in-the-wild RGB(D) video---into an adaptable dexterous skill. At the core of AdaDex is Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking: a shared policy is trained on two populations of massively parallel environments: motion tracking environments trained with dense motion tracking objective, which instill the human prior from human motion; and generalization environments with noised initial states and goals and a sparse object-success reward, which force the skill to work far off the reference. From seconds of human motion per skill, the resulting policies can learn diverse adaptable dexterous skills, such as functional grasping, object reposing, in-hand reorientation with finger gaiting, and dynamic behaviors like throw-and-catch. Our method outperforms baselines in terms of generalization and functionality, and we demonstrate transfer across simulators and to the real world. Project page: https://yuxuank.com/AdaDex/.

articles.title: UniWALM: Unified World Action Language Model for Embodied Robot Control
articles.content: Motivated by the human ability to integrate experience across language, perception, and action, we introduce UniWALM, a unified world-action-language model that learns video, action, and language in a single shared representation, where each modality is both a conditioning signal and a supervision target. We ask: can jointly generating language enrich this shared representation, improving manipulation and supporting memory-dependent behavior? Unlike prior approaches that attach a reasoning or vision-language model to a video-action backbone and run them as distinct stages, UniWALM unifies all three modalities inside a single mixture-of-transformers backbone whose per-modality diffusion heads co-denoise synchronously, decoding subtask and textual memory in the same pass as action with no separate planning stage; the generated language is re-consumed on the next step, closing a language-as-memory loop without an external planner or memory bank. To keep the action stream reliable under this richer objective, we further introduce Flow Matching with Correction (FMC), a training objective that teaches recovery from perturbed action trajectories at no inference-time cost. UniWALM consistently improves over same-backbone baselines (e.g., FastWAM) on compositional pick-and-place (MolmoSpaces) and across the memory-dependent subset of RMBench, where it reaches 34.5% without any pretrained language or reasoning model and exceeds Mem-0's keyframe-equipped setup (28.5%) using only a single anchor frame. On a real-world Find-the-Item task, generating textual memory lifts success from 11.1% to 61.1%, while state-of-the-art VLAs stay at or below chance (<=33.3%).

articles.title: PsycheMME: A Psychology-Informed Benchmark for Social Understanding and Interaction in Videos
articles.content: Understanding human needs and selecting responses require distinct judgments that aggregate accuracy can obscure. We introduce PsycheMME, a video benchmark informed by psychology, with eight capabilities spanning grounding, states, needs, interaction decisions, memory, and risk. Drawing on Social Information Processing and the Perception-Action Cycle, this organization separates human understanding from response selection. We construct 1,000 questions from 630 episodes through independent answering with proposed references withheld and expert review. Our Reasoning-Verified protocol weights answer credit by the support and logical consistency of explicit rationales against annotated cues. Across 17 models, Timing has the lowest Verified scores and credit retention, with weaker support judgments for correct Timing answers. Models with similar Need scores still differ in answer completeness on open questions. Input controls and SFT/GRPO examine context dependence and adaptation. Evaluating answers alongside rationales locates where models fail across understanding, response selection, and justification.

articles.title: Industrial ReMEmbR: Scaling Spatiotemporal Memory to Robot Fleets
articles.content: Warehouse robot fleets continuously observe operational conditions, but preserving these observations as reusable semantic memory incurs substantial computation, communication, and storage costs. For example, explaining recurring aisle blockages can require reviewing video from multiple robots across several shifts. We present IndustrialRemembr, a shared spatiotemporal memory system that extends NVIDIA ReMEmbR to robot fleets and reduces server-side computation by generating scene descriptions only on demand. On each robot, an NVIDIA Jetson encodes video clips into retrieval embeddings with Cosmos-Embed1, vision tokens with Cosmos3-Edge, and reconstruction latents with the Wan2.2 VAE, without uploading raw camera frames. The encoding models are re-used to detect people in image patches, zeroing them out to support PII abstraction for GDPR-compliant deployments. We split Cosmos3-Edge at its vision-language boundary, placing the vision encoder on the robot and the language decoder on an on-premises server. A Nemotron agent retrieves memories by content, position, and time and queries the decoder using cached vision tokens. This design eliminates caption generation at write time, while cached-token decoding reproduces the unsplit model's output in all 450 tested decodes.

articles.title: Planning under Noise with Neural Operators
articles.content: Planning under uncertain control execution noise requires reliable feedback policies across diverse environments. We introduce Planning Under Noise (PUN), a neural operator that learns noise-aware value fields for planning in unseen geometries. Building on an established screened-Poisson formulation of stochastic optimal control, we address two challenges: specifying boundary conditions that support navigation across varying geometries and efficiently computing fields with reliable gradients. Zero-Dirichlet obstacle boundaries terminate sampled paths at walls, weakening the goal signal along long routes and making it harder to estimate reliably. We instead impose reflecting Neumann conditions on obstacles and a Dirichlet condition at the goal, allowing sampled paths to continue exploring free space until they reach the target. To solve the resulting PDE without a configuration-space mesh, we extend a Monte Carlo (MC) solver, Walk on Stars (WoSt), to higher dimensions. However, local MC fluctuations can reverse estimated gradient directions and cause planning failures, making direct planning require costly sampling. PUN amortizes this computation by learning geometry-to-field mappings from noisy, partially converged Monte Carlo labels, avoiding expensive convergence for every training example. At inference, test-time scaling uses bounded local search guided by the predicted global field. We evaluate PUN on planning tasks across dimensions. Across four noise levels, PUN matches or outperforms all compared planners, achieving 95-100% success on the 4D replanning benchmark while maintaining the lowest runtime. At the highest tested noise level in 4D, PUN achieves 10.7-60.6% relative gains in success rate over other methods while running 3.29-32.15 times faster.

articles.title: MindView: Benchmarking Generative Multi-View Spatial Intelligence
articles.content: Spatial intelligence has recently been assessed through generative tasks such as spatially grounded image editing, yet language-guided generation of spatially consistent views from partial multi-view observations remains underexplored. We introduce MindView, a benchmark for generative multi-view spatial intelligence with 1,500 samples from 513 scenes across three indoor datasets. Its seven tasks form two families: geometry-dominant tasks specify changes in camera position and orientation, while semantics-dominant tasks require inferring target viewpoints by grounding referred objects and interpreting spatial relations and reference-frame cues. Evaluation of eleven generators reveals substantial room for improvement on MindView. A paired context analysis further shows that all eleven generators obtain lower overall scores under the expanded context setting. These findings motivate us to investigate whether task-specific supervision can improve target-view generation and whether models can use additional multi-view evidence effectively. We therefore fine-tune BAGEL on the MindView training dataset, improving its overall score by 24.3 points and yielding gains across all seven MindView tasks. Beyond these generation gains, the fine-tuned model also yields higher scores on three spatial-understanding benchmarks without training on their annotations, suggesting that learning to generate spatially grounded views may benefit spatial understanding. To improve evidence utilization under expanded context, we propose MindCue, a training-free spatial evidence selector guided by a target-view hypothesis. MindCue reverses the drop in overall score under expanded context and outperforms the standard-context baseline. Overall, MindView provides a concrete testbed for generative multi-view spatial intelligence.

articles.title: Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction: How far should we go?
articles.content: Multi-token prediction (MTP) can accelerate language-model decoding by drafting several tokens and verifying them in a single target-model pass. However, the best speculation horizon changes with context: longer drafts offer greater amortization when reliable, but can waste compute on suffixes discarded after a rejection. Unlike autoregressive drafting, where a stopping rule can decide token by token, MTP must fix the horizon before drafting, as all heads fire in the same forward pass. We therefore formulate horizon selection as an online control problem, using verification feedback to learn how far the draft can be trusted in each context, and introduce Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction (AMTP): a lightweight controller that requires no retraining and leaves the exact verifier unchanged. To guide horizon selection, we characterize the expected number of tokens committed at each horizon via acceptance survival, the probability that a draft prefix is fully accepted. Before each round, AMTP predicts how far the draft is likely to survive and picks the horizon with the highest expected tokens per second, learning freely from every verification pass. Theoretically, we show that any online learner's prediction error translates into throughput regret against the best horizon for each context, and in turn into a bound on wall-clock completion time. With online gradient descent, this regret is sublinear. Across five draft-target pairings built on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with Medusa heads, Meta's MTP models, and Qwen3-4B-Inst-2507-MTP, evaluated on AIME 2025 and GSM8K, AMTP decodes up to 4.1x faster than standard decoding and matches or outperforms the fixed window in 8 of 10 settings, with throughput gains of up to 10%.

articles.title: Efficient Edge-aware Attention Network for Graph Generation
articles.content: Graph generative models commonly use graph-specific Transformer architectures to jointly update node and edge features. However, these architectures do not directly benefit from recent hardware-aware attention implementations, limiting their scalability. The adaptation is, however, non-trivial: edge and graph-level features must be injected into pairwise attention scores, graph masks must be respected, and dynamic edge updates remain a major source of quadratic memory usage. We propose an edge-aware attention layer for graph generation that incorporates structural information through head-wise score modulation, while updating edge representations with a lightweight residual mechanism that retains attention-score dependent edge updates. This layer can be effectively implemented using PyTorch's FlexAttention. We achieve similar generation quality to our baseline while reducing peak GPU memory by around 65% and substantially improving training and sampling throughput. These results suggest that the proposed architecture is a practical step toward scalable graph foundation models.

articles.title: NarraSpace: Multimodal Scene-Grounded Evidence for Picture-Description Dementia Classification
articles.content: Picture-description dementia classification uses a shared visual scene, but a transcript-level prediction alone does not identify the scene evidence underlying its inputs. NarraSpace links words and speech times to named picture elements and retrieves utterances for predefined scene events. Narrative-spatial descriptors summarize coverage and temporal organization. A frozen language model contrasts each event's text under examples from Alzheimer's disease and healthy-control training participants, alongside transcript surprisal and coverage measurements. Retained source records link event scores to their source utterances, speech intervals, and lexical matches. On the official 48-participant test set of the Alzheimer's Dementia Recognition through Spontaneous Speech benchmark, a fixed support vector classifier achieves $80.88\%\pm2.56\%$ mean accuracy over fifty seeds; averaged probabilities yield $81.25\%$ accuracy and $91.32\%$ area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. NarraSpace makes the construction of scene-linked classification inputs explicit and inspectable by connecting event-indexed language-model measurements to their source utterances, speech timing, and extraction records. Such source-linked measurements could support clinician review of picture descriptions by presenting quantitative summaries alongside the original speech evidence.

articles.title: KoalaGS: Complexity-Aware Continuous Level of Detail for Gaussian Splatting
articles.content: Deploying a trained 3D Gaussian Splatting scene under shrinking compute budgets requires one primitive set to remain effective when rendered at smaller prefixes. In this continuous level of detail (LoD) setting, the challenge is to decide which Gaussians should retain capacity as the budget decreases. A pilot study on 3DGS-MCMC reconstructions shows that image complexity, computed from the input views before optimization, predicts where reconstruction error concentrates in image and 3D space. It also reveals that simple regions contain too many Gaussians and degrade as much as complex ones at lower budgets, despite being inherently cheaper to represent. Subsequently, in KoalaGS, during training we use this complexity prior to bias relocation toward poorly reconstructed areas while ensuring smooth degradation across LoDs. A primitive importance score then enables inference at low-capacity, while preserving the scene structure. Tested across three datasets, KoalaGS maintains competitive full-capacity quality while significantly improving quality across the budget spectrum, yielding smoother transitions across LoDs, and enabling faster progressive streaming.

articles.title: Physical Canvas: A Vision Tactile World Model For Robot Policy Evaluation And Learning
articles.content: Evaluating and post-training robot policies through physical interaction is costly and difficult to scale, motivating action-conditioned world models as interactive simulators. However, visually plausible predictions can misrepresent contact dynamics, providing unreliable feedback for policy evaluation and learning. We introduce PhysCanvas, a state-consistent visuo-tactile world model for contact-rich robot manipulation. PhysCanvas unifies multi-view RGB, tactile images, marker displacement, task state, and actions within a unified vision space. All modalities share a video VAE and pretrained generative backbone, allowing optical touch to reuse visual and temporal priors. Motion images derived through forward kinematics and camera projection provide spatially aligned action conditioning, while an initial RGB anchor and updated reference observations guide sequential generation. Our consistency-aware post-training uses the frozen Scene Reward Model, Modality Reward Model, and State Reward Model to supervise scene preservation, visual-tactile compatibility, and agreement with real task outcomes. The resulting world model supports closed-loop policy rollouts for evaluation and provides imagined interactions and rewards for GRPO policy updates. Across four real-world manipulation tasks, when policies are rolled out in the world model, State Reward Model supervision increases the arithmetic mean of task-wise Pearson correlations between world-model and real-world success rates from 0.602 to 0.885. Policy post-training in the reward-guided world model further increases $π_{0.5}$'s mean real-world success rate from a 59.1% SFT baseline to 70.8%. These results demonstrate the value of unified multimodal modeling and consistency-aware post-training for robot policy evaluation and learning. Project page: https://zebinx.github.io/PhysCanvas_HomePage/.
